title: Decide whether Binding.scalars and Binding.rows should preserve the element type
description:
`Binding.scalars` takes an `Executable` and returns `list[Any]`; `Binding.rows` returns `Sequence[Row[Any]]`. A caller writing `binding.scalars(select(Customer))` gets `list[Any]` rather than `list[Customer]`, so nothing downstream of the query is checked.

The generic form that would carry the element type through is spelled differently across the supported range: `Select[tuple[T]]` on SQLAlchemy 2.0, `Select[T]` on 2.1. The dependency is `sqlalchemy>=2.0.21` with no upper bound, so a single spelling is wrong on one side of that range.

Options:

- Pin `sqlalchemy>=2.0.21,<2.1` and use the 2.0 spelling. Callers get real types; the project takes on an upper bound and the work of lifting it later.
- Leave the signatures as they are. No upper bound, no false precision, and callers annotate at their own call sites when they care.
- Look for a spelling that holds across both, or overloads selected by a `TYPE_CHECKING` version test. Worth a short spike before committing to either option above.

The design posture on a pre-1.0 project favours the cleanest end state over compatibility with our own past, but an upper bound on a dependency is a cost paid by every downstream install, not just by us.

Done when the decision is recorded here and either the pin plus generic signatures land, or this ticket is closed as deliberately unchanged.

title: Annotate remaining functions and enable mypy disallow_untyped_defs
description:
The mypy configuration runs with `check_untyped_defs`, `warn_return_any`, `strict_equality`, `no_implicit_optional`, `warn_redundant_casts`, and `warn_unused_ignores` on, but `disallow_untyped_defs` and `disallow_incomplete_defs` off. Bodies are checked; signatures are not required to be complete.

Turning both on reports 29 functions in `src/` needing annotations, concentrated in `cli.py` (subcommand handlers taking a bare `args`), `runtime/binding.py`, `runtime/history.py`, and `db.py`. Most are mechanical — `args: argparse.Namespace`, `-> None`. The SQLAlchemy-facing ones in `runtime/` need more care because the useful types are generic.

Done when both flags are on in `pyproject.toml` and `./check.sh` passes.
close_reason: Signatures completed; both mypy flags on and check.sh green

title: Establish agent working conventions, pre-push check script, and CI
description:
Set the repo up so agent work follows the documented working agreement.

Deliverables:

- `CLAUDE.md` capturing the working agreement, with project-specific sections filled in (overview, key files, commands, architecture, reference library).
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` with a checklist covering the check script, tests, changelog, docs, and the tracked issue.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running the same steps as the local check script.
- `./check.sh` — one command running ruff format, ruff lint, mypy, and pytest, with a `--quick` mode.
- `scripts/lint_prose.py` — fails on process labels in persistent artifacts and on over-long changelog entries.
- `CHANGELOG.md` with an `[Unreleased]` section.
- Dev dependency group and tool configuration in `pyproject.toml`; line length 79.
- Reformat existing sources to 79 columns.
- Branch protection on `main` with the CI check required.
close_reason: Conventions, check script, prose lint, CI, and PR template landed

title: Keep dependencies and workflows updated with Dependabot and audited with zizmor
description:
Two supply-chain gaps: nothing proposes dependency or GitHub Actions updates, and nothing checks the workflows for the usual Actions security mistakes.

Add `.github/dependabot.yml` covering the `uv` ecosystem (`pyproject.toml` plus `uv.lock`) and `github-actions`, both weekly with a 7-day cooldown so a release has to survive a week before it is proposed. Group each ecosystem into a single pull request so a week of updates is one review rather than five.

Add `zizmor` to the dev dependency group and a step to `check.sh`, so workflow auditing runs locally and in CI through the same script as every other check. Fix what it reports on the existing workflow: pin both actions to commit hashes with the version in a trailing comment, set `persist-credentials: false` on checkout, and declare explicit `permissions`.

Action versions stay where they are; Dependabot proposes the major bumps on its own schedule.
close_reason: Dependabot config and zizmor step landed; workflow findings fixed
